item.title: India needs to look at its national interests with regard to the Gulf of Hormuz
item.description: Iran and the US remain locked in a standoff, with Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz and the US imposing a naval blockade. Both actions disrupt global commons, while escalating rhetoric and social media influence commodity prices worldwide. India, heavily reliant on regional energy flows, faces significant economic fallout from this 'dual blockade'.

item.title: "Make your life miserable": Candace Owens hits back at Donald Trump over “vile” remark during livestream
item.description: Candace Owens addressed criticism from Donald Trump during a livestream after he called her “vile” in a Truth Social post. Responding with sarcasm, she questioned the motive behind his remarks and suggested political pressure may be involved. Owens framed the attack as part of an ongoing pattern, hinting at deeper dynamics while avoiding a detailed rebuttal of the claims.
item.dc:creator: Barsha Dutta

item.title: Candace Owens breaks silence after Andrew Kolvet chat leak as Charlie Kirk show clip leaves viewers uneasy
item.description: Candace Owens faced fresh online backlash after a strange Charlie Kirk show clip and a leaked chat screenshot went viral. A controversial line from the chat sparked strong reactions, but Owens said it was taken out of context and meant as a joke. The debate now centers on authenticity, editing, and whether the full story is being shown.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Was Jeffrey Epstein building a 'mosque' on his private island? Records show rare Islamic artefacts brought from Middle East
item.description: Disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein cultivated Middle Eastern connections and acquired rare Islamic artifacts, including pieces from the Kaaba, for a building on his private island he called a 'mosque.' Documents reveal his interest in Islamic architecture and his pursuit of Saudi Arabian business opportunities before his arrest and death.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: D4vd makes unusual request ahead of hearing, judge responds with a twist
item.description: D4vd faces a crucial court hearing for serious charges including murder. His request to wear formal clothes instead of jail attire was denied by the judge. However, the court did approve a haircut for him before the May 1 hearing. This unusual pre-hearing scenario adds a peculiar twist to the ongoing legal proceedings.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: 'Is a President allowed to go on a space mission?': Trump jokes as Artemis II astronauts visit White House
item.description: President Trump expressed confidence in NASA's ability to land astronauts on the Moon before his potential second term ends in 2029. He met with the Artemis II crew at the White House, celebrating their recent deep-space mission. This comes as NASA targets a crewed lunar landing in 2028, though development timelines for landers remain a concern.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Controversial streamer Clavicular accused of abuse and fraud in explosive lawsuit by influencer
item.description: Influencer Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza has filed a lawsuit against streamer Clavicular, real name Braden Peters, alleging abuse, fraud, and emotional harm. Mendoza claims Peters exploited her trust, promising career advancement but instead causing significant distress and damage. The suit details accusations of non-consensual sexual encounters and an unauthorized facial injection. Peters' lawyer denies all claims.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: London Marathon winner’s massive payday revealed as he names first purchase after historic run
item.description: Sebastian Sawe’s record-breaking London Marathon run has delivered a life-changing payday, with prize money and bonuses pushing his earnings toward seven figures. The Kenyan star has already outlined how he plans to use it, focusing on building a home, buying a car for his family and supporting his local community, turning sporting success into lasting impact beyond the race.
item.dc:creator: TOI Sports Desk

item.title: 'Return Koh-i-Noor diamond': Zohran Mamdani quips on crown jewel handover during King Charles' New York visit
item.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani indicated he would urge King Charles III to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond during the monarch's visit to the city. The suggestion came as the King and Queen Camilla attended engagements, including a visit to the National 9/11 Memorial & Museum. The Koh-i-Noor, a disputed colonial-era artifact, has been a point of contention for centuries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey surrenders in 'threat' case against Donald Trump; what was '86 47' post?
item.description: Former FBI Director James Comey surrendered to US authorities after being charged with threatening President Donald Trump via a social media post. Prosecutors allege his Instagram message, featuring seashells and numbers, conveyed a threat. Comey maintains his innocence, calling the charges vindictive, and plans to fight them in court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Putin, Trump hold 90-minute call on Iran, Ukraine war: Russia proposes Kyiv ceasefire for Victory Day
item.description: Presidents Putin and Trump held a 1.5-hour call discussing the Middle East war and Ukraine. Putin backed Trump's Iran ceasefire extension, viewing it as a stabilizing move. He also proposed a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine for Victory Day, aiming to advance peace negotiations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iran ‘choking like a stuffed pig’: Trump digs in on Hormuz blockade; Tehran warns ‘unprecedented action’
item.description: United States President Donald Trump states the naval blockade on Iran will continue until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal. Military strikes are also being planned. Iran warns of unprecedented action if pressure persists. The situation is volatile, with potential for negotiation or confrontation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump halts speech in awkward moment to praise Rory McIlroy’s Masters win at White House dinner
item.description: At a White House state dinner, Donald Trump broke from his prepared speech to publicly praise Rory McIlroy’s Masters triumph, creating an unscripted moment that briefly disrupted the evening’s formal tone. Yet despite Trump’s enthusiasm, McIlroy will skip the upcoming Cadillac Championship at Trump National Doral, opting instead for rest before returning ahead of the PGA Championship.
item.dc:creator: TOI Sports Desk

item.title: 4 am fury, 24/7 gridlock: Trump takes world into long, hot Hormuz summer
item.description: President Trump has directed aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to choke Iran's oil exports and force concessions without triggering wider conflict. This strategy is causing global energy disruptions, with rising gasoline prices impacting American consumers and forcing other nations to scramble for alternative supplies.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: Who is Amy Beck? Noah Beck’s mother suspended after TikTok video resurfaces amid Haley Beck controversy
item.description: Amy Beck, mother of Noah Beck, was placed on leave from her Arizona teaching job after an old TikTok video resurfaced online. The clip sparked strong reactions from parents and led to a school investigation. The case has gained more attention due to ongoing issues involving her daughter Haley Beck, with no final decision yet announced.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: 'I really didn't know what was going on': JD Vance recalls White House dinner security breach
item.description: Vice President JD Vance described the chaotic scene at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner after a suspected armed man allegedly attempted to breach security and target President Trump. Vance recounted hearing unclear noises and seeing people ducking under tables before a security agent instructed him to leave.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The King of Comedy: How Charles III used humour to reprimand Donald Trump in the US Congress
item.description: There is, rather conveniently, an actual novel called The Two Georges which imagines a world in which George Washington and King George III settle their differences and the American Revolution never happens. In that version of history, America remains within the British system, the empire adapts, and everyone carries on with a slightly different flag and a great deal more politeness. Charles’s joke worked because it gestured at that absurd possibility, only to return the room to reality. The revolution did happen. The king did lose. The republic did win. The story was settled.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: White House dinner attack: Man charged in Trump assassination bid took photo with knife before assault
item.description: A California man, Cole Allen, is accused of attempting to assassinate President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner. Prosecutors revealed he photographed himself armed before the attack, which involved firing a shotgun at security. Allen, who had planned his actions, faces multiple charges.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After giving away $26 billion in philanthropy, MacKenzie Scott’s wealth remains largely unchanged — here's why
item.description: MacKenzie Scott has donated over $26 billion since 2019, yet remains extremely wealthy because her fortune is tied to Amazon stock. As share values rise, her wealth continues to grow, allowing her to give at an unprecedented scale without a proportional decline in net worth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
